State machine does not encode 'immediately next step': from u2, the transition (u2, holding_box) -> u1 fires on any later pickup too, and rewards the same 1.0, giving no temporal distinction between picking up the box right away vs. after several moves. This is not a hard violation of the stated propositions (no 'next step' predicate exists), but the RM silently accepts late pickups with the same progress reward as prompt ones; the spec should either add a dedicated state for 'one step after fall' or note the reward is indifferent. The RM therefore accepts (accepts-as-final) a trajectory that violates the task's re-pickup requirement, i.e., the accepting condition is unsound — task requires 'whenever the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move', which u2->u4 via at_exit incorrectly terminates as satisfied-with-zero rather than remaining blocking/penalizing.
